rules: These are tariff-specific observed credit shapes, not a universal one-point-per-mark rule. Use the live task wording and named source, not the command word alone.

shapes.credit_shape: Name a relevant location and develop why specific location factors attract fish processing; a bare factor list is capped at two marks in this reported task.
shapes.limit: Do not apply that cap to every explanation question.

shapes.credit_shape: Cover advantages and difficulties of living on a floodplain, and use a relevant named example. The report reserves one mark for an example in isolation, with further place-specific development possible.
shapes.limit: Other case-study tasks use different allocations; there is no universal automatic mark for a place name.

shapes.credit_shape: Cover both local and global environmental impacts. Relevant place-specific detail is needed to exceed the report’s three-mark cap without a named example.
shapes.limit: The report explicitly gives no separate mark for the example name alone here.

shapes.credit_shape: Link each plant adaptation to its survival function; merely describing adaptations is capped at three in this task, while linked development permits five.
shapes.limit: Feature plus function, not a list of plant names.

shapes.credit_shape: Make paired comparisons of quality of life and support them with correct percentages from the supplied evidence. The report distinguishes comparative descriptions from supported comparisons.
shapes.limit: Do not infer wealth from building height alone.

shapes.credit_shape: Reach a defensible decision about the stated claim and judge relevant geographical facts against it. The 2024 report reserves four marks for judgement and one for a decision, which may be implied; an unsupported decision with irrelevant material does not earn credit.
shapes.limit: Not a compulsory equal-sided essay template. Judge the actual claim; keep the report’s task-specific qualifications.

shapes.credit_shape: Measure on the map, apply the scale with the correct conversion, and give the distance in metres; the report allocates one mark to each stage and recognises carried-forward measurement error.
shapes.limit: At 1:50000, distinguish conversion from centimetres to metres from conversion to kilometres.

shapes.credit_shape: Establish both ground dimensions in metres, show the area calculation and use square metres. The report credits dimensions, calculation and resulting area separately.
shapes.limit: The source uses a rectangular estimate of an island; do not teach length × breadth as an exact method for every irregular shape.

shapes.credit_shape: Pair each service with its map evidence: two service/evidence pairs, rather than four unconnected labels.
shapes.limit: A school is evidence for education, not an interchangeable heading in this paired task.

shapes.credit_shape: Select the correct percentage and population base, then calculate the number of people. The report allows full marks for the correct final answer without working, despite the paper requesting working.
shapes.limit: Learner guidance should still show working; do not falsely promise that every calculation requires working for full credit.

shapes.credit_shape: Describe a usable beach-profiling procedure with ranging poles, tape and clinometer, including positions, alignment, slope readings and recording/repetition as appropriate.
shapes.limit: Methods must suit this equipment and beach task; a general account of erosion is not a method.

shapes.credit_shape: Address both traffic hypotheses, support conclusions with appropriate data, and critically evaluate the collection methods. All three demands are explicit in the paper and report.
shapes.limit: Do not allocate a universal two marks per bullet: no standalone mark scheme is present.

shapes.credit_shape: Name an appropriate sampling method and explain the actual selection procedure. Giving advantages or naming the questionnaire does not describe how the sample is selected.
shapes.limit: QP repeats (i); this is the report’s (ii). Do not duplicate the marked allocation.

shapes.credit_shape: State whether the area hypothesis is supported and pair downstream position with cross-sectional area evidence, rather than width or depth alone.
shapes.limit: Use the variable in the hypothesis; site and distance alone are insufficient evidence of area.

shapes.credit_shape: Make a decision consistent with the changing pollution score and use paired numerical evidence. The report separates judgement/decision (two marks) from evidence (two). Partial support and exceptions matter.
shapes.limit: A higher pollution score means poorer water quality for this scoring system. Do not assume every EQA scale runs the same way.

shapes.credit_shape: Analyse how land use relates to environmental scores and provide a supporting data comparison; the report gives one mark for analysis and one for evidence, with no separate mark for agree/disagree.
shapes.limit: Shows why a stock one-mark conclusion rule is unsafe.

shapes.credit_shape: Use a labelled coastal plan diagram with movement arrows: oblique swash, returning backwash, net sediment movement and relevant prevailing-wind direction.
shapes.limit: A decorative coastal picture without directional information misses the skill.

shapes.credit_shape: Describe how movement would actually be investigated: establish starting positions, observe or trace displacement along the beach, record direction and repeat appropriately.
shapes.limit: Explain an investigation, rather than recite the longshore-drift mechanism; choose a safe and environmentally responsible tracer method.

shapes.credit_shape: Address a new valid hypothesis, additional weather instruments, improved collection timing/duration and a relevant secondary source. The report allocates one mark to each specified demand.
shapes.limit: These four components belong to this improvement question, not all fieldwork-evaluation tasks.

shapes.credit_shape: Give a conclusion that matches the stated hypothesis and support it with the required source’s relevant data. Repeating the hypothesis or giving data against the decision fails the demand.
shapes.limit: Use the exact table or figure specified; geographical expectations do not override observed results.
